name: Banana plant
doc: a banana plant: a green pseudo-stem with big torn paddle leaves (kampong gardens, roadsides)

name: Bicycle
doc: a bicycle, upright (a messenger's, a soldier's or a nurse's bike, a village policeman); people ride it with "rides": "bicycle"

name: Coconut palm
doc: a tall coconut palm with a curved ringed trunk, a crown of feathery fronds and a bunch of coconuts (groves, kampongs, beaches)

name: Estate road with tall grass
doc: a red laterite road through a rubber estate, tall lalang grass in front (a watcher can hide in it)

name: Estate road (open)
doc: a red laterite road through a rubber estate, open to the camera (columns, cyclists, convoys)

name: Army field kitchen
doc: army field kitchen (a two-wheeled wagon with a soup kettle and a smoking chimney): soup queues, cooks at the front, soup kitchens at home

name: Japanese field cap with neck flaps
doc: the Imperial Japanese Army field cap (senjo-bo): soft khaki cap, short visor, yellow star, cloth neck flaps hanging to the shoulders

name: Jungle edge (rainforest wall)
doc: a stretch of dense tropical rainforest seen from its edge: tall trunks with buttress roots, lianas, layers of dark foliage, ferns at the foot; put several side by side for a wall of jungle

name: Deep jungle in mist
doc: inside dense rainforest in mist: giant trunks and leaves (the jungle of legend)

name: Kampong (Malay village)
doc: a Malay village among coconut palms: houses on stilts, banana plants, a red road

name: Kampong house (Malay house on stilts)
doc: a Malay village house raised on wooden stilts: plank walls, shuttered windows, a steep thatched (attap) roof with a gable, wooden steps up to the door

name: Lalang (tall grass clump)
doc: a clump of tall lalang grass (waist high): roadsides and clearings; a row of it in front hides a watcher

name: Malayan town street (shophouses)
doc: a street of Chinese shophouses with coconut palms and a red laterite road

name: Notice board
doc: a notice board on two legs with pinned notices (ration announcements, call-up orders, casualty lists) — set "text" on the card's paper_note for the exact words

name: Parang (machete)
doc: a parang: the heavy Malay machete used to cut through undergrowth (held in the hand)

name: Jungle edge
doc: where a plantation meets the rainforest: a dark wall of jungle behind open ground

name: Road through a rubber estate (gap for a position)
doc: a laterite road through rubber with a gap in the near trees: room for a roadblock or a gun position

name: Rubber estate (rows of tapped trees)
doc: inside a Malayan rubber estate: straight rows of tapped rubber trees in the humid haze

name: Rubber tree (tapped)
doc: a tapped rubber tree: slim grey trunk with the diagonal tapping cut and a latex cup, a light crown high up; plant it in straight rows (Malayan rubber estates)

name: Sandbag wall (low)
doc: a low wall of stacked sandbags (three courses, waist high): a roadblock, a gun position, the front of a trench

name: Sarong (checked kain pelikat)
doc: a checked cotton sarong wrapped at the waist and falling to the ankles (Malay, Tamil, Burmese men); recolour it in the cast

name: Chinese shophouse
doc: a two-storey Chinese shophouse of a Malayan town: a covered five-foot way with pillars and the open shop behind, shuttered windows above, a tiled roof, a red signboard; put several side by side for a street

name: Shovel
doc: a long-handled shovel for digging trenches and gun pits (held in both hands; drawn around the hand)

name: Sikh turban (dastar, khaki)
doc: the Sikh soldier's wrapped turban, folds crossing to a point over the forehead (Indian Army: khaki); give the person a beard

name: Singlet (vest top)
doc: a white cotton singlet: the scoop neck and arm holes (give the person outfit robe, color #efece2 and armColor = skin colour)

name: Tropical beach (landing)
doc: a sandy tropical beach with coconut palms and the sea: landings, dawn arrivals

name: Australian slouch hat
doc: the Australian Army slouch hat: khaki felt, dented crown, puggaree band, the left brim turned up with the Rising Sun badge

name: Songkok (Malay velvet cap)
doc: the black velvet songkok, flat-topped and oval, worn by Malay men (villagers, clerks, policemen, aristocrats)
